title: ADBC drivers, Arrow results, DuckDB SQL
description: Use a standard database-client API to connect DuckDB to different backends. ADBC exposes Arrow batches; each driver determines its underlying protocol and conversions.

sections.title: Arrow at the client interface
sections.description: ADBC drivers expose query results and bulk ingestion through Arrow. The extension reads batches into DuckDB without requiring CSV exports or intermediate files. This does not imply that every database speaks Arrow over the network.

bulletPoints.label: One API, multiple databases
bulletPoints.description: Use installed ADBC drivers for SQLite, PostgreSQL, Flight SQL, and other supported backends. Available features depend on the driver.

bulletPoints.label: Native libraries
bulletPoints.description: Resolve drivers through installed ADBC manifests or load a shared library by path. Drivers run inside DuckDB with the process's privileges.

sections.title: Catalogs and explicit command handles
sections.description: Choose a read-only attachment for analytics and an explicit handle for remote SQL and transaction control. Both can target the same shared database.

bulletPoints.label: Catalog queries
bulletPoints.description: ATTACH with TYPE adbc and READ_ONLY exposes remote schemas and tables with supported projection/filter pushdown. The catalog pools connections for independent scans.

bulletPoints.label: Runtime commands
bulletPoints.description: Use standalone CALL adbc_execute, CALL adbc_commit, and CALL adbc_rollback. Command side effects happen at execution, not during PREPARE or ordinary EXPLAIN.

bulletPoints.label: Schema metadata
bulletPoints.description: adbc_scan uses ExecuteSchema, or an explicit columns declaration when unsupported. adbc_scan_table and adbc_schema obtain named-table metadata through GetTableSchema.
